::: {.lead}
This is a self-study series and reference codebase building up the foundations of agentic AI — bandits, MDPs, RLHF, tool use, planning, retrieval, calibration — from the ground up.
:::

Every algorithm is derived from first principles, implemented in under 500 lines of NumPy or PyTorch, and motivated through a **probabilistic lens**. Decision-making, exploration, retrieval, and reflection all turn out to be approximate inference problems in disguise; the series makes that explicit.

If you've trained a neural network and read a few RL or Bayesian inference papers, you're the target reader.
